theme.title: Courtside Curiosities
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 2018–19 champion Raptors win?
questions.context: Toronto · Kawhi Leonard's lone Raptors season
questions.note: 58 wins, earning second place in the East.

funFacts.text: Toronto exchanged DeMar DeRozan, Jakob Poeltl and a protected pick for Kawhi Leonard and Danny Green.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: DeMar DeRozan (who spent his first nine seasons in the NBA with the Raptors)

funFacts.text: The Raptors added Marc Gasol from Memphis at the trade deadline for a package led by Jonas Valančiūnas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Memphis Grizzlies traded Marc Gasol to the Raptors

funFacts.text: Nick Nurse was promoted from assistant coach after Toronto dismissed Dwane Casey.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Raptors promoted assistant coach Nick Nurse as their head coach

questions.prompt: As an eighth seed, Miami beat Milwaukee in 2023. How many points did Jimmy Butler score in his career-high game in that series?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: scoring a career-high 56 points in a 119–114 victory

funFacts.text: Miami upset Milwaukee, whose regular-season record had made the Bucks the clear betting favorite.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they faced the Milwaukee Bucks, the team with the best record in the league

funFacts.text: Tyler Herro broke his hand and Victor Oladipo tore a knee tendon in the opening playoff series.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they lost starter Tyler Herro in game 1 with a broken hand

funFacts.text: Butler later won the East finals MVP as Miami held off Boston's attempted reverse sweep.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Butler was named the Eastern Conference finals MVP

questions.prompt: Over 19 seasons, how many games did John Stockton miss?
questions.note: Just 22. He played every game in 17 seasons.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: missing only 22 games in his 19-season career and playing every game of 17 seasons

funFacts.text: Stockton had completed 17 full seasons without missing a single game.
His most significant injury was a left-knee MCL problem that kept him out at the start of 1997–98.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: due to an injured MCL in his left knee sustained in the preseason

funFacts.text: He was still Utah's starting point guard when he retired at age 41.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He remained a starting NBA player until his retirement at age 41

questions.prompt: How many points per game did Chris Webber score for the 2002 Kings?
questions.note: 24.5 points per game despite missed time.

funFacts.text: Webber also pulled down 10.1 rebounds a game.
His passing added another 4.8 assists per game.
He made the All-NBA Second Team that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: and was named to the All-NBA Second Team

questions.prompt: What is the NBA record for points in a Finals game, set by Elgin Baylor in 1962?
questions.context: Los Angeles Lakers vs Boston Celtics · 1962 NBA Finals

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Baylor set the still-standing NBA record for points in an NBA Finals game with 61.

funFacts.text: Baylor helped turn basketball into a vertical spectacle; later high-flying stars modeled their moves on his.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Baylor introduced a creative and acrobatic playing style that would later be emulated

funFacts.text: Seattle University eventually named its basketball court for Baylor, honoring the former college star.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: they named its basketball court in honor of him

funFacts.text: Although Baylor retired before the Lakers' breakthrough, the team presented him with a championship ring.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Lakers did give Baylor a championship ring for his contributions at the start of the 1971–72 season
